tasks.title: manifest-based managed sync in install.sh
tasks.intent: Installs must be upgradeable: re-running install.sh delivers updated templates without clobbering user edits.
behavior: Given a fresh project, when install.sh runs, then all templates are copied AND .github/.envoy-copilot-manifest.json records each installed file's content hash
Given an installed project where a template changed upstream and the local copy is unmodified, when install.sh re-runs, then the file is overwritten and the manifest updated
Given a locally-edited managed file, when install.sh re-runs, then the file is left untouched and a 'locally modified, skipped' warning names it
Given a pre-manifest install, when install.sh re-runs, then files identical to current templates are adopted as managed; differing files are treated as user-edited
acceptance: install_file gains manifest logic; summary counts installed/updated/skipped-modified
Symlink mode unchanged (symlinks not rewritten or manifest-tracked)
Hermetic Node test execs install.sh into temp dirs: fresh install, no-op re-run, upstream-update re-run, user-edit preserved, pre-manifest adoption

tasks.title: stack-instruction drift-guard + backfill the Azure five
tasks.intent: Nothing notices when stacks/ and the Copilot instruction templates diverge; make drift a test failure and close the existing 5-file gap.
behavior: Given a stack profile without a matching .instructions.md template (or vice versa), when the suite runs, then the drift-guard test fails naming the missing counterpart
Given the 5 Azure stacks, then each has a condensed instruction file with a correct applyTo glob
acceptance: Drift-guard asserts bidirectional 1:1 between stacks/*.md (minus detect-stacks.sh) and instruction templates
The 5 new instruction files follow the existing condensed style (applyTo frontmatter, no Detection blocks)
